vulnerabilities.description: No input validation on memory keys. Attacker could inject special characters or path traversal sequences. Keys are written directly to JSON without sanitization, and could be exploited if memory.json is parsed by other systems.
Memory file stored in unencrypted plaintext at .claude-flow/data/memory.json. No access control or permission checks. Any process with filesystem access can read/modify sensitive context data.

Unsafe file path resolution for package.json. No validation that resolved paths are within expected directories. Could potentially read arbitrary package.json files if directory traversal is possible.

HTML parsing with node-html-parser without output sanitization. If parsed JSON-LD or HTML content is later used in a web context, could enable XSS. Currently low risk (CLI-only) but dangerous if repurposed.

baseUrl() function allows override via FREEHIRE_API_URL environment variable without protocol validation. Attacker could redirect to HTTP endpoint: `FREEHIRE_API_URL=http://attacker.com` to perform MITM attacks.
Hardcoded User-Agent string is outdated (Chrome 120.0). While not a security risk, hardcoded User-Agents can be detected and blocked. Should use a real browser User-Agent or rotate dynamically.
Session file stored as plaintext JSON at .claude-flow/sessions/current.json. Contains context and metrics that could be sensitive. No encryption or access control.

recommendations: Add input validation and sanitization for all keys in memory.js — use whitelist of allowed characters (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores only)
Encrypt sensitive data in memory.json and session.json files using Node.js crypto module with a derived key from a master secret
Implement strict permission checks (chmod 600) on .claude-flow/data/memory.json and .claude-flow/sessions/current.json to prevent world-readable access
Validate that FREEHIRE_API_URL uses HTTPS protocol: `if (!baseUrl().startsWith('https://')) throw new Error('HTTPS required')`
Use URL constructor validation: `new URL(baseUrl())` to ensure valid URL format
If HTML parsing output is ever used in web contexts, sanitize with DOMPurify or similar; add security comment noting current CLI-only status
Validate resolved package.json paths are within allowed directories using path.resolve() and pathname checks
Add JSDoc security warnings on functions that accept environment variable overrides
No hardcoded API keys detected (✓ Good) — maintain this practice
Review and audit all dependencies in package.json using `npm audit` and `snyk` for known vulnerabilities
Consider adding security headers validation for HTTP responses (check for X-Content-Type-Options, etc.)
